title: Edge Guard Keeper — proto jot
content:
Problem summary (quick):
We have customers running Redwood Private/edge proxies that occasionally experience noisy/long-lived sessions which: 
- consume KV cache aggressively,
- hold GPU slots during intermittent spikes,
- leak identities across short-lived worker restarts (rare),
- and make safe rollbacks hard when a model variant misbehaves.

Goal / north star:
A lightweight, deployable 'Edge Guard Keeper' that sits in the edge worker process (or sidecar) and enforces session-level safety/economy rules with minimal perf impact. Provide observable controls and safe rollback primitives so product teams can ship conservative defaults then tune per-customer.

Success metrics (example):
- 30% reduction in median KV pressure for targeted customers in 30 days.
- Reduced tail GPU contention incidents (P99 queue-time) by 15% for edge region X.
- No customer-visible increase in median latency (>5% allowed).

Primary use cases / user stories (raw):
1) As an SRE I want an automated evictor that reclaims stale conversation context after configurable inactivity so that KV cache doesn't fill with zombie sessions.
  - Criteria: per-tenant TTL; soft-hint eviction first; hard eviction with audit log.
2) As a Platform PM I want a circuit breaker for model variance regressions so that we can auto-fall back to a verified variant if error-rate or hallucination-rate spikes.
  - Criteria: quality signal threshold, rolling window, fallback mapping.
3) As a Customer Admin I want to define a per-user budget for tokens/requests so the edge doesn't let a single user exhaust reserved capacity.
  - Criteria: user quota counters, rate-limit response semantics documented.
4) As an Engineer deploying Private I want a low-friction toggle to enable Edge Guard in dev and prod, with safe dry-run telemetry and canary controls.

Core components (sketch):
- Guard daemon (embedded library or sidecar): lightweight, <15ms added p95 latency on hot path.
- Policy engine: simple DSL (JSON) for TTLs, eviction priority, circuit thresholds, fallback map. Keep intentionally minimal to avoid full PDP complexity.
- Local store: small in-memory LRU to track session heartbeats + persistent audit stream (append-only) to object store for forensics.
- Telemetry hooks: counters + traces; events emitted for policy triggers.

Example policy (informal):
{
  tenant: "acme-corp",
  session_ttl_minutes: 90,
  eviction_strategy: ["soft-prune-prefix", "hard-drop-after-ttl"],
  circuit_break: {error_rate_pct: 4, window_minutes: 5, fallback_model: "redwood-2-small"}
}

Instrumentation / telemetry to ship with v0: 
- metrics: guard.evictions_total, guard.evictions_by_reason, guard.circuit_trips, guard.latency_added_ms{p50,p95,p99}.
- traces: include trace id linking request -> guard decision.
- logs: event record for each hard eviction and circuit trip (structured JSON).
- debug-only endpoints: /guard/dryrun?tenant=xxx -> returns decisions without mutating state.

Operational concerns / constraints: 
- Security: policies must be stored encrypted in KMS when persisted. Access controls: customer admins vs platform operators.
- Performance: keep policy eval O(1) amortized; avoid any blocking network call on the request path.
- Storage: audit stream retained per tenant for 30 days by default (configurable).

Rollout plan (quick):
- alpha: embed guard in internal staging edge for 2 internal teams (one high-throughput, one test). Dry-run only. 2 weeks.
- canary: enable enforcement (soft) for 1% of customers in one region. Monitor metrics. 1–2 weeks.
- ramp: 10% -> 50% with progressively stricter defaults and user quotas. 4–6 weeks.
- GA: opt-in for Private customers, default-off for hosted. Provide migration guide.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Policy JSON can be pushed via local config and validated.
- Guard emits telemetry and dry-run endpoint returns consistent decisions.
- Basic eviction (TTL) works without request latency regression >5% median.
- A documented rollback path: flip off guard or switch to fallback model mapping.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes-to-self):
- DSL: full-featured policy language vs minimal predicates. Start minimal (TTL + thresholds) and iterate.
- Where to evaluate policies? In-process cheap check vs remote policy server (latency + single point of failure). Lean in-process for now.
- Interaction with Dedicated autoscaling: evicting sessions could change demand signals; need SRE sync.
- Customer expectations: when we evict a session, do we return a graceful response to client? Insert small in-band header/metadata to explain eviction and next steps.

Edge cases to log for next design pass:
- Multi-worker session ownership (we may need a lease token).
- Long-lived streaming sessions: avoid killing mid-stream without a graceful pause point.

Next immediate steps (TODO):
- Draft an ADR for in-process policy eval (owner: Maya). Due: 09/20.
- Spike: implement proof-of-concept guard as a library that can be toggled by env var. (owner: Sam) 2-week spike.
- Telemetry: add metrics scaffolding to edge-worker StatsD + tracing hooks. (owner: Lucas)
- Customer comms: write small doc for Private customers explaining opt-in and expected behaviour. (owner: Product)

Quick links / refs (scratch):
- Slack thread: #private-onboard (link -> search)
- Jira INF-4532 (design spike)
- GH draft: infra/pull/1123 (guard sidecar scaffold)
summary: Sketch for an in-edge safety/economy guard to reclaim resources and provide rollback/fallback behavior for Private/edge deployments. Focused on TTL eviction, circuit-breakers, quotas, and observability.
